title: Quick Revision: Sound

bullets: Sound is produced by a **vibrating** object. In humans, sound comes from the vibrating vocal cords in the **larynx** (voice box).
Sound needs a **medium** (solid, liquid or gas). It cannot travel through a vacuum.
We hear when sound makes the **eardrum** vibrate; the vibrations are passed on to the inner ear and then to the brain.

table: Number of vibrations per second, in hertz (Hz)
Time for one vibration, in seconds

box: Human hearing: about **20 Hz to 20,000 Hz**. Below 20 Hz is infrasonic; above 20,000 Hz is ultrasonic (dogs can hear some of it).
Sounds above about **80 dB** become physically painful.

bullets: Unpleasant sounds are **noise**; pleasant sounds are music.
Sources of noise pollution: vehicle horns, loudspeakers, firecrackers, machines, construction work.
Effects: lack of sleep, high blood pressure, anxiety, and even loss of hearing.
Control: silencers on vehicles and machines, keeping TVs and music low, planting trees along roads, keeping factories away from homes.
